A1.justification: The supplied PDFs are readable and describe the same work, with MiCL renamed OCL. Their algorithms, equations and retained experiments align. V1 ends after its references; v2 includes Appendices A–B, which were also inspected.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet-1K classification, efficiency and ablation results in Figure 3 and Tables 2–6.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports dense-prediction and distribution-shift results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: Renaming MiCL to OCL does not change the procedure: randomly masked, non-overlapping patch groups pass through a shared ViT, and normalized CLS features are trained with T-SP similarity and symmetric contrastive loss. Algorithm 1 retains the same operations.

E1.justification: The supplied v1 reports ImageNet-1K evaluation. V2 additionally reports COCO object detection and instance segmentation, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch distribution-shift evaluations (Tables 7–8). This substantially broadens the represented tasks and test conditions.

E2.justification: Table 6 removes the SimCLR v2 comparison. The new comparisons in Tables 7–8 introduce evaluated baselines absent from v1, including supervised pre-training, DenseCL, GreenMIM, EsViT, MixMAE, SimMIM and MSN.

E3.justification: V2 adds Mask R-CNN and UperNet evaluation protocols, AP and mIoU metrics, and ImageNet-source domain-generalization testing. COCO evaluation specifies 1024×1024 inputs and 16×16 windows. Table 6 also changes reported epochs: OCL 800 to 1,600, ConMIM-L 1,600 to 800, and iBOT-L 1,200 to 1,600. OCL's new table entry conflicts with the retained 800-epoch description; these reporting changes do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit robustness and generalization tests on ImageNet-A, ImageNet-R and ImageNet-Sketch in Table 8. These examine performance under distribution shifts beyond v1's masking-ratio, batch-size, MLP-head and concentration-parameter ablations, whose numerical results are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 7–8 add substantial results: OCL-L reports 53.2 box AP, 47.0 mask AP and 53.2 mIoU; OCL-B reports 42.2%, 52.3% and 37.6% accuracy on ImageNet-A/R/Sketch. Retained ImageNet accuracy and ablation values are unchanged. Table 6 omits the SimCLR v2 and MAE-H/14 entries previously reported there.

T1.justification: The architecture definitions, cosine similarity, T-SP transformation and contrastive-loss equations retain the same mathematical content. V2 adds no theorem, proof, substantive derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: semantic views from masking, contrastive pre-training without reconstruction or auxiliary modules, and efficient scaling. The headline 133-hour, four-A100, 85.8% result is unchanged; the new name and future-work outlook do not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: V1 Section 4.2.2 distinguishes actual mini-batch size from effective batch size and says gradient accumulation did not improve performance. V2 Section 3.2.2 replaces this with an effective-batch explanation involving expanded negative pools, despite unchanged scores. V2 also adds interpretations concerning dense-task scalability, robustness and stable convergence.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link and Appendix B with optimizer, learning-rate schedule, weight-decay, FFN and downstream-training details in Tables 9–11. However, Table 3 removes actual mini-batch sizes. New documentation also conflicts with the main text: Table 9 gives a ViT-L batch size of 2,400 versus 2,048, and Table 11 gives 90 ViT-B probing epochs versus 100.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work to Appendix A, v2 substantially expands coverage of methods such as latentMIM, data2vec, MaskCo, MSCN, RECON and CMAE. New Section A.4 identifies MSN as the closest work and explicitly differentiates OCL from MSN, ExtreMA and CAN.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and method terminology throughout, rewrites substantial introduction and explanatory passages, moves related work from the main text into Appendix A, and adds an implementation appendix and concluding outlook. This substantially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to one column throughout. Table 6 is redesigned with separate ViT-B/ViT-L result columns, Table 3 loses its actual-batch column, and Tables 7–11 are added. The three existing figures are retained and repositioned, with some labels and captions revised.

improvement.justification: V2 adds valuable transfer and robustness evidence, implementation details and closer engagement with prior work. However, it removes the actual-versus-effective-batch qualification without changing the supporting scores and introduces conflicting budgets (1,600 versus 800 epochs) and batch sizes (2,400 versus 2,048). These problems affect the central efficiency argument and reproducibility, leaving the net effect of broader evidence and weaker reporting uncertain.
